explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 26 sits near 1 at GO/D2 and dips mainly at D1, increasingly so late in the episode (timing R^2 0.65). Beyond timing, magnitude is set at D1 by the previous trial's outcome: it drops most after a1->S2 rewarded (rare rewarded, -0.30), also after a2->S2 rewarded and a1->S2 unrewarded, and rises after S1 unrewarded (+0.11..0.13) and after a2->S1 rewarded; roughly an S2-looks-good evidence signal (low z = more updating). These last-trial effects grow strongly in the final ~20-30 trials of the episode (interaction terms with an exponential late ramp and ep_dec>=7). Small extras: GO-phase policy logit (slightly lower z when favouring a1) and a small positive D1 correction when S2 was rewarded two trials back (partial reversion of the last-trial effect). Last-trial D1 table alone: dev 0.55; with late-episode scaling 0.60-0.63; full 6-term set dev 0.645, test 0.64 (ceiling all 0.64). Good state, trials since reversal and future cues add ~0.01.

issues: 'Lowered after S2 rewarded' is driven mostly by a1->S2 rewarded, which is a RARE transition. In fits by episode decile at D1, a1 S2 r gives -0.28 in deciles 0-6, while a2 S2 r (common) gives only -0.056 in deciles 0-6 and reaches -0.20 only in decile 9. The rare/common asymmetry is large and the label does not mention it.

Late-episode amplification is not a uniform scaling of A. a1 S2 r barely grows (-0.28 -> -0.35 -> -0.38 -> -0.34 for deciles <=6/7/8/9) and a1 S2 u also levels off (-0.08 -> -0.12). Meanwhile S1-unrewarded grows 3x (a1 S1 u +0.088 -> +0.265, a2 S1 u +0.10 -> +0.32) and a2 S2 r grows about 3.5x. So the 'amplified late' claim holds only roughly.

Part of the late growth is a reward main effect, not the S2-good signal. Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_reward==1)*exp((ep_trial-99)/8) to the 6 terms raises test R2 from 0.641 to 0.651, which beats the 0.64 additive ceiling.
The GO choice terms are called 'small extras', but they add about 0.03 test R2 (0.610 without them, 0.641 with them). The D1 2-back term adds about 0.011 (0.599 -> 0.610).

The worst-fit windows are mostly the first D1 of a window, where the previous trial is unknown ('?'). The model predicts about 0.55 there, but the actual value ranges from 0.13 to 0.9. This is a limit of the window data, not an error in the label.

No large systematic error class remains. In misses, the largest per-(phase, previous trial) mean errors are within +/-0.024 (D1 after a2 S2 u +0.024, GO after a1 S2 u +0.018). The test score of 0.641 reproduces and matches the ceiling.
